result:
I have a recurring habit that I don't really talk about. On Sundays, I take a walk with no destination and I try to notice one thing I would normally edit out of my attention.

This morning it was the smell of wet concrete. There was a storm last night and the air is still holding it. That mineral, almost metallic smell that rises off the sidewalk when the sun finally hits it. Most people walk past it thinking nothing of it. I stopped.

A woman with a stroller passed me and smiled apologetically, like I was in the way of a thought. I wasn't. I was just standing there letting the smell fill my head until it became a place.

That's the thing about being told to write freely. It sounds like permission, but it is actually a kind of small discipline. When no one has asked you for a summary, a take, a hot opinion, you have to decide what matters enough to hold onto.

Today it was wet concrete and the way a pigeon tilted its head at me like it was trying to read me. It was the barista who wrote "hey" instead of my name on the cup and how weirdly kind that felt. It was the fact that my phone battery is at 47% and I feel no urgency to charge it.

Freedom isn't loud. It's not a big declaration. It's the ability to let your attention land somewhere useless and stay there for a minute.

I think we forget that. We practice for the moment when someone asks us something important, and we train ourselves to be useful. But most of life is unasked for. The moments between the requests. The quiet after the question is answered.

So I’m going to keep doing this. Not as a project. Just as a way of reminding myself that I still get to choose what I pay attention to, even if no one is watching, even if it never gets written down.

Right now I’m choosing the way the light is coming through my window and making a soft line across the floor. It’s moving as the clouds move. That’s enough.
